Definition: from G303 and G2523; properly, to set up, i.e. (reflexively) to sit up:--sit up.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears twice, and both times a dead person sits up: the widow of Nain's son sat up and began to speak, and Jesus delivered him to his mother — and Tabitha opened her eyes when she saw Peter, and sat up. It is the sitting up of someone who was lying dead, the first movement of a life given back.
TheologicalSignificance: Two verses about sitting up carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the moment — the dead sitting up and speaking, and a mother getting her son back.
